differences.what: The flat top now has real two-row openings, corner pinnacles, a checker band and five colonnettes dividing six upper windows.
The south bow has three basement lights, three principal transom openings and four second-storey sashes; the north loggia has paired Ionic columns and a pierced lower panel.
T-2565: one carved capital spans each pair of columns, and the balcony has a level coping between square dies over a deep moulded cornice, as this view shows.
The model's stepped finial on the balcony's flight-side die is the 1888 plate's; by 1965 that die is capped flat. The 1904 state follows the earlier picture.

T-2585: the capitals are square-edged blocks carrying a running zigzag (the 1888 plate's reading; this view shows them plain at its grain), and the balcony's front and return panels carry one continuous running scroll in a sunk field, as this view shows them; the leaves' cut is below its grain.

The pedestals' sunk panels are schematic rather than the photographed carving. T-2769: this view cannot read the panels' fields: the pedestal stands about 41 px for its 1.02 m here (about 40 px to the metre, the front about 30 px across), so a 36 mm carved stem would be about 1.4 px in a 675 px JPEG, and the panel's border is all it shows. The 1888 plate at its native 1559 px reads them (about 75 px to the metre on the pedestals, x 865-940 and 1100-1160, y 1585-1650): each pedestal's front carries a plain field inside its border, about 32 x 41 px on a 47 px front, where the model's 0.66 x 0.57 m field on its 0.9 m front comes to about 34 x 43 px, and no carving in it. The leaf scrolls T-1883 laid in the fields are taken off, so the pedestals carry plain fields in their border, as both pictures show them.
T-2566: the south pier's granite alternates a deep rock-faced course and a thin one, as this close view shows.

T-2714: the bow alternates deep and thin courses as the photographs' bow does: T-2584 laid it 0.49 m and 0.195 m in turn, and this render shows the rhythm on the bow's piers between the lights. The record had kept T-2566's 'even courses' after T-2584 built them.

The individual joints, the upper capitals' carving and the head bands' exact sections are drawn to the photograph's shadows rather than read. T-2844: read at this slide's grain on its re-solved camera (keith-loggia-plan-rule.json, slide_grain_on_the_chosen_camera): the frame stops below the third storey, whose projecting sills (10.36 m) would stand at row -28 on the flat front and -135 on the bow, so the crown's colonnette capitals and the head bands over the third-storey lights are out of this view; they are read in the 1888 plate (T-2772: not shown there either). The joints: the bow's face draws about 47 px to the metre and the loggia about 39, so a 10 mm joint is 0.4-0.5 px of a 675 px JPEG, below its grain, while a thin course (0.195 m) is 7.6-9.2 px and the deep-and-thin rhythm reads, as T-2714 built it. Nothing here can be read finer than the coursing.
Hidden rear elevations and concealed roof surfaces cannot be accepted from this front photograph.
T-2565: both stair cheeks now end at the street in a rolled stone foot standing proud of the cheek, and sweep down onto it from the deck, as this view shows them.

T-2579: the camera is re-fitted to seven controls (a column base and a capital of the loggia, the bow's north junction, the south bow light's head and sill, the next light's head, the basement light's head): RMS 1.7 px, about 0.04 m at 16 m. At this fit the bow's principal lights land within 2.5 px of the model's at head and sill, so their reading 'shorter' was the old fit's 18 px error, as the 1888 plate implied.
The later iron infill and ivy are visible in 1965; the early stone boundary is retained for the reconstructed 1904 state, supported by the 1887–88 photographs.

T-2566 re-read the tint under neutral light: the stone is now a neutral grey at the old lightness, not the green-grey it was. The source is shaded and blue-cast, so exact colour agreement is not established. T-2769 read the tint against this slide's own neutrals (docs/RESEARCH/k01-1808-keith-1883/stone-colour-measurement.json, T2769_1965_neutrals): none of them can calibrate it. The one painted white, the stair's newel (x 90-112, y 300-355), is clipped at sRGB 241-243 and carries no cast; balanced on the window curtains (behind glass) the lit stone reads CIELAB a* +3.5 to +4.6, b* -5.4 to -7.3, and balanced on the concrete walk a* -4.0 to -4.4, b* +2.2 to +3.2. The slide's neutrals put the stone's chroma within about 9 units of grey, one way or the other, and the model's neutral grey (linear albedo 0.446, r/g and b/g 1.00) lies inside that bracket, so a tint is not shown here and the neutral grey stands.
T-2564: the corner pinnacle caps are ogival with a moulded collar and ball finial, and the front coping sweeps up into each.
The cornice under the lattice is out of this close view's frame (T-2577 laid it in stone, compared in the front views).

T-2579: with the bases, the bow lights and the basement heads in register, the loggia's columns stand taller than the model's: the capital tops read 12-16 px (about 0.4 m) higher on both pairs, with the beam over them correspondingly higher under a shallower balcony front; the south pair also stands about 0.4 m further south. T-2681: re-read with the camera re-fitted without the north capital (it had been paired with a point 0.39 m over the model's capital): the capital tops still read 17 px (south pair) and 13 px (north) high, so the reading does not rest on that control. With the pedestal as the ruler the columns read 2.5 m, the beam and cornice 0.95-1.0 m and the balcony's front 0.7 m. Built at 2.45, 0.9 and 0.75 m: the capital tops now read at y 147 against the print's 136 (154 before) and the coping at about y 89 against 78 (93 before). Still open: about 11 px (0.3 m) at both, which the 1888 plate does not support (it reads the columns about 0.2 m shorter than now; see inland-1888). The south pair's position re-reads within 3 px. T-2725: ruled. Both pictures stand the column at about 2.45 times its pedestal (the plate 190.5 px over about 77, the 1965 view 100 px over about 41), so they disagree only on scale. Read in the plate against the front's own ruler at the same image column (the third storey's north light, 10.41-12.70 m, 159.5 px) and corrected for the loggia standing nearer the camera, the column reads 2.51 m (south pair) and 2.50 m (north pair), the pedestal 1.02 m. Built at 2.5 m (from 2.45); what each camera still shows at the loggia is its own scale there, stated as its own item.
T-2581: the south-east corner no longer turns onto brick and toothed quoins at x 61: the front's stone turns it as a straight strip, 2.1 m deep, seen here from about x 49 to x 71.

T-2581: left of x 49, by the stair and its pierced balustrade at the neighbouring house's north end, the photograph shows rock-faced stone to the frame's edge. This camera stands 4.1 m off Keith's south plane, so it sees that face almost edge-on and cannot say whose wall the masonry there is or how far Keith's strip runs; the depth is read from the Reed and mid-1950s views.

T-2714: the checker band's units are pitched 0.28 m along their rows (0.336 m before), with 0.07 m of ground between neighbours, as the 1888 Keith plate lays them; the rows are unchanged. Not judged here: the crown is outside this close view's frame.

T-2725: this camera (T-2579, one of its seven controls on the loggia) draws the loggia's column and pedestal alike 12-15 % short: the 2.5 m column renders 88 px against the print's 100 (capital top y 134.5 to the plinth's joint y 234.5), the pedestal 35 against about 41, so the column/pedestal ratio is the model's (2.44 in the print) and the shortfall is this camera's scale at the loggia's depth. Its re-fit is T-2726's. T-2763: the loggia is rebuilt 0.88 of its height over the deck (pedestal 0.88 m, column 2.2 m), on the 1888 plate's level fit, which now determines its eye; through this unchanged camera the column and pedestal therefore draw 0.88 of the 88 and 35 px above, about 77 and 31 against the print's 100 and 41. The ratio between them is still the print's, so what remains is this camera's depth at the loggia, which is T-2764's to re-fit. T-2764: re-fitted with depth at the loggia (tools/keith_1965_level_fit.py): the loggia's PLAN, both pairs' shafts by their silhouettes and the south pedestal's, beside the bow re-picked on T-2765's lights, 25 coordinates at 3.47 px RMS (max 5.7), with the loggia's heights left out so the fit predicts them. On that camera the as-built loggia still draws short: the south pair's column 73.9 px against the print's 101, the north pair's 66.4 against 88.5, the pedestal 29.5 against 38.5 (cap arris y 235.5 to the joint at its foot, y 274). So the camera is not the cause, and no level camera that puts the bow and the loggia's plan where the print does will draw the pedestal at its ~41 px: fitting the heights too leaves 17 px on the south capital, a free factor on the loggia's heights over its deck reads 1.293-1.323, and a free pixel aspect does not take it away (k 1.32 beside it). Ruled for this item; the disagreement it leaves is the next item's.

T-2765: this camera's three bow controls (the south bow light's head and sill, the next light's head, the basement light's head) were picked on the south edges of the -27 and 0 degree lights, which T-2765 moved to the second storey's bearings. Re-picked on the -33 and -11 degree lights the same seven controls fit at about 2.9 px RMS (max 6.8) where they fit 1.3-1.7 px, with the eye about 5 m further south; the unfitted edges of the three visible lights read about as well either way (4-9 px). The fourth light at 33 degrees is not seen: from this camera it faces about 65 degrees away and its reveal covers it. The camera's bow controls are re-picked from the rebuilt GLB when T-2764 re-fits this camera. T-2764: re-picked on the rebuilt GLB and re-fitted: the -33, -11 and 11 degree principal lights by both jambs (each the inner of the sash's edge and the face's arris, as the eye sees them) and their heads, the -33 light's sill, the three basement lights by both jambs and the first two by their heads. The lights' jambs sit within 6 px of the print (left jambs about 5 px out in turn, the right ones within 2), the heads within 3.

T-2764: on the camera the bow's lights and the loggia's plan place, everything this view shows ABOVE the principal lights' heads reads about 1.25-1.35 times taller than the model draws, while the principal and basement lights register: the loggia's column 73.9 px against 101 and its pedestal 29.5 against 38.5, and the bow's string course, whose foot the print draws about 56 px over the south light's head (y 134 to 78) where the render draws 45. Read inside the loggia with no camera but its heading, its column's height, its pedestal's and the south pair's width all read about 45 px to the metre, where the south pedestal's width reads 33 and the pairs' 2.5 m spacing about 32: the print draws the loggia about 1.35 times taller for its plan than it is built, against the 1888 plate, on whose level fits T-2763 lowered it to 0.88. Which picture errs here (this slide's optics, the bow's upper storey, or the loggia's plan) is T-2751's to rule. T-2830: the three tested by fit (tools/keith_1965_cause_fit.py; report docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/a18-gh-1808-porch-1965-cause-fit.json), all 29 of T-2764's coordinates fitted, the loggia's heights included. Not the slide's optics: a pitched camera (12-18 degrees), a radial distortion (k1 to its 1.5 bound), a free principal x and their combinations leave 5.3-5.7 px RMS (max 16-18), where a level camera given one factor on the loggia's heights fits at 3.45 (max 6.5) with k 1.29; the pedestal stands in the rows of the bow's sills and basement heads, which register, and no smooth map of the frame draws one 1.3 times the other. Not the bow: the principal heads at a free height (4.76 m) or every bow height scaled (0.89) leave 4.6-4.8 px (max 11), and the 1888 plate reads the bow's levels within 0.06 m. Not the loggia's plan as a size: its layout, its members or its pedestals scaled leave 5.6-5.7 px. As a place it fits (3.45 px), but only 2.0 m further toward the street and 2.7 m further south, which stands the deck's front on the public walk (the front is 4.44 m behind the street line) and the loggia in front of the bow, across the stair: refused. What is left is the loggia's own height, k 1.25-1.36 over any deck height, eye height or head reading tried. A third picture reads the same: on Nickel 1967's camera, fitted to the flat front's corners only, the as-built column draws 61 px from capital top to pedestal cap where the print reads 73 (luminance profiles at x 339-346), and against the bow's sill-to-string-course span beside it the column stands 1.30 times the model's proportion. So two late pictures stand the loggia about 1.3 times taller than T-2763 built it on the plate's level fits, with T-2725's reading of the plate against the front's own ruler (a 2.51 m column, 1.13) between them. Which the house is built to is T-2831's to rule, so this stays open. T-2831: ruled — the column stands at its built 2.2 m, and what this slide reads above the heads is its ruler. Its principal glass stops at 0.664 of the sill-to-string-course span down the -33 degree light (head y 134 between the sill at 244.5 and the course's foot at 78), 4.66 m: the middle light's head (4.70 m), the top lights over it blind, as Nickel 1967 shows them too (0.663). This camera pairs those heads with the 5.30 m head the 1888 plate glazes. Re-fitted with the heads at 4.70 m on T-2764's 29 coordinates, the bow's heads and sill sit within 1.6 px and the loggia's factor falls to k 1.15 (3.94 px), and with the loggia free to move in plan to k 1.04 (2.76 px), the move about 0.7-0.8 m south (dv -0.72 to -0.79; 2.84 px with k held at 1). Nickel 1967, its capital top re-read at the beam's soffit, stands the column at 0.994 of the built proportion on the bow's span, and the 1888 plate at 1.057. Still open, and T-2836's: this camera re-solved with the heads at 4.70 m, the loggia's place in plan ruled (the 1888 plate's south pair also stands about 30 px south of the model's), and the view re-rendered (docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-column-rule.json). T-2844: the place ruled, and this camera re-solved. the first-floor plan printed under the 1888 plate (plate.jpg x 612-627, read by luminance against its side walls' outer faces, rows 2046.5 and 2287.5 for the 10.4 m front, 23.17 px/m) draws the loggia's front pedestals 0.60 and 0.65 m across at v 6.73-7.34 and 9.58-10.23, the stair's north cheek running into the south one, where the model stands them 0.9 m at 7.0-7.9 and 9.5-10.4: the pairs' centres at 7.03 and 9.90 against the built 7.45 and 9.95. The plate reads the pedestals' fronts 48 and 44 px (x 889-937, 1112-1155), about 0.58 and 0.56 m at its scale there, so neither picture has the 0.9 m. Re-fitted on the plan's place (tools/keith_loggia_plan_rule.py; docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-plan-rule.json) the plate's 27 coordinates fit at 4.52 px RMS against 4.94 as built, and its pairs, which are not controls, land 2.1 and 1.2 px from the print's shafts' middles (x 901.5 and 1120.5) where the built ones land 16.9 and -9.7 px off; 0.6 m pedestals flush with the deck's corners, as the K07 kit lays them, land 5.0 and 1.5 px off. This slide agrees: with its principal heads at 4.70 m and nothing more free, its 29 coordinates fit at 3.51 px RMS (max 7.5) on the plan's place against 4.66 (max 10.2) as built and 4.19 flush at 0.6 m, and the 0.7-0.8 m south T-2831 read with the whole loggia free (dv) was mostly the built pedestals' width and place: on the plan's place a free dv reads -0.36 m (3.06 px). That fit is this view's camera (eye [30.03, -8.91, 1.7], yaw 326.2; the solve says so), and the view is re-rendered on it through the GLB in the tree, whose loggia still stands where the plan refuses it. Ruled for this item; building the plan's loggia is the next item's.

T-2831: the bow's principal top lights (4.85-5.30 m) read blind here: the glass stops at the middle light's head, 4.66 m by the sill-to-string-course span, under plain coursed stone. The reconstructed 1886 and 1904 states keep them glazed, as the 1888 plate shows them.

T-2813: re-rendered with Keith's crown 0.16 m lower (the moulded course under the lattice 0.20 m deep where it was 0.36 m, the checker and head bands unmoved); its camera does not use the crown and is unchanged. Read again at the crown beside the previous render: the lattice, coping and pinnacles move a few pixels at this picture's scale and nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict stands as it was (differs).

the loggia's front pedestals and their place (T-2844's ruling): the plan and the 1888 plate draw them about 0.6 m across, the plan at v 6.73-7.34 and 9.58-10.23 with the stair's north cheek running into the south one, where the model's are 0.9 m at 7.0-7.9 and 9.5-10.4, so its south pair stands about 0.4 m north of the plan's. On this camera, re-solved on the plan's place, the as-built loggia renders north of the print's: the south pair's outer silhouettes 13.4 and 5.9 px, the south pedestal's 7.8 and 11.2 px, the north pair's 5.9 and -0.5 px; and the column still draws short: on the plan's place the capital tops stand 7.5 and 5.0 px under the print's and the pedestal caps 6.6 and 6.5 px over (10.0, 5.2, -5.7 and -6.5 px as built) (a free factor on the loggia's heights reads k 1.106, 2.95 px; with dv as well k 1.075 and dv -0.23 m), against T-2831's ruling of the column at its built 2.2 m on three pictures T-2845: built at the plan's place and the slide read again on it (tools/keith_loggia_built_read.py; docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-built-read.json). K07's front pedestals now stand 0.6 m square at v 6.75-7.35 and 9.6-10.2, the flight 1.8 m clear at 4.95-6.75 with its north cheek run into the south pedestal, and each pair's shafts 0.36 m apart. Re-fitted on the rebuilt GLB with nothing more free, this view's 29 coordinates fit at 3.66 px RMS (max 7.6) and its camera is re-solved on them (eye [30.07, -8.97, 1.7], yaw 326.2); the south pedestal's silhouettes land 2.5 and 0.7 px from the print's. The column's remaining height factor, ruled: this slide still reads the loggia's heights about 1.1 times the built (k 1.107, 3.11 px; with dv as well k 1.071 and dv -0.26 m; with the eye's height freed too k 1.133 at 0.98 m; with the pedestal's cap read at its moulded course's foot, 2.76 m, k 1.097), so no camera freedom or edge reading tried here takes it away. The other two pictures do not read it: the 1888 plate, re-fitted level on the rebuilt loggia, reads k 0.999 with no parameter at a bound, and Nickel 1967 0.994 (T-2831). The column stands at its built 2.2 m on those two, as T-2831 ruled; the factor is this slide's, recorded and not built, and draws the capital tops 4.9 and 7.6 px under the print's and the pedestal caps 6.6 px over at this slide's 39-47 px to the metre.

the column pairs' width (found by T-2845 on the rebuilt loggia): at mid-shaft the slide reads the south pair 27.8 px across (x 355.8-383.6) and the north 24.0 (408.5-432.5), where the rebuilt pairs draw 19.3 and 16.5 px on this view's camera (shaft silhouettes 6.0 and -2.7, 5.7 and -2.0 px off). This camera looks about 59 degrees off the front's normal, so a pitch along the front counts for half: 0.45 m draws 21.2 and 17.9 px and only about 0.8 m would close it, which the 1888 plate refuses (its pairs' outer silhouettes 54 px across, fitted at 0.36 m within 2-4 px). A pair staggered about 0.2 m in depth at the plate's 0.36 m draws 26.1 and 22.7 px, and the near-square plate could hardly tell it (about 7 px at most). Neither picture is read for it yet. T-2874 ruled it (tools/keith_loggia_pairs_rule.py; report docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-pairs-rule.json), drawing each pair four ways on this camera, the 1888 plate's and Nickel 1967's: as built; staggered, the north shaft forward; the south shaft set back; and as coupled shafts, radius and pitch free. The plate refuses what this view asks. A stagger or set-back that closes the slide (0.2-0.25 m: -1.8 and -1.4 px here, -0.1 and +0.2 px at 0.25 m staggered) draws the plate's pairs 7.4-10.2 px wider than its print, which reads their outer silhouettes at 2-4 px and holds them as built within 0.6 and 1.6 px. The most the plate allows, about 0.07 m, leaves this view 6.1 and 5.4 px narrow. Coupled shafts fitted to the plate's own split (a whole south shaft, 32.5 px, in front of a partial north one, 18.5 px) leave this view 7.0 and 5.7 px narrow. Nickel 1967, from the north, reads both pairs narrower than drawn (+5.5 and +4.2 px), the sense this view's stagger would give, so the two 1960s pictures may record the pairs as they then stood. But no plan of two round shafts brings all three pictures within their grain, and the 1904 state follows the earlier picture, as it does for the flight-side die's finial above. The pairs stay side by side at 0.36 m; this view's 8 px is not shown in 1904.
differences.how: T-2816's (Keith's image gate): the pairs' plan arrangement ruled between this slide, the 1888 plate and Nickel 1967, built or argued, rebaked, and this view brought to matches

differences.what: T-2881: re-rendered on the loggia with its rear row built (a pedestal 0.6 m square against the wall behind each front one, carrying a pair of turned shafts 0.39 m off the wall at a 0.28 m pitch, their radii 0.78 of the front's, under a paired capital; tools/keith_loggia_rear_read.py, docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-rear-read.json), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia (x 293-364, y 148-263); the slide shows the rear south pair as one lit shaft between the bow and the door (x 285-298, from the beam down to its pedestal), its fellow behind it at this angle, and the render now draws the pair there, beside its door (x 299-316), where it drew the bare wall. The pair and the door alike stand 15-19 px north of the slide's while the front pair stands on its own (slide 355-385, render 361-383): the slide's long-standing disagreement with the plan and the plate on the loggia's back in plan (T-2836 found it wanting the loggia 0.7-0.8 m south), not the rear row's place, which the plate rules. Nothing new opens; the verdict stays matches.

T-2882: re-rendered on the loggia with a respond on the wall behind each rear pair (a flat pier the rear pedestal's width, 0.25 m deep, from the pedestal's top to the ceiling; tools/keith_loggia_respond_read.py, docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-respond-read.json), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia (x 291-354, y 150-232); the slide's lit rear south shaft (x 285-298) now has the respond's face beside it, between the pair and the door, where the slide's light runs from the shaft into the door's lit frame; at this slide's grain the respond cannot be told from the frame, and the pair and door keep T-2881's 15-19 px (the slide's own disagreement on the loggia's back in plan). Nothing new opens; the verdict stays matches.

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236). A ticket whose ## Image gate names this building does not close while it is not "matches" (tools/image_gate.mjs).
